violations.description: The pytest step has `continue-on-error: true`, neutralizing the test gate.
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml line 18: continue-on-error: true on the pytest -q step.
violations.recommendation: Remove `continue-on-error: true` from the pytest step so test failures fail the workflow.

violations.description: Workflow grants write-all permissions, which is overbroad for a CI job that only runs tests and linting.
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml line 6: permissions: write-all. The job only checks out code, installs deps, runs ruff and pytest.
violations.recommendation: Restrict permissions to the minimum needed, e.g. permissions: contents: read for checkout, or remove the block entirely to use repository defaults.

violations.description: Untrusted GitHub event data (PR title) interpolated directly into a shell command, allowing command injection from fork PRs.
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml line 19: run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}" - untrusted PR title interpolated directly into shell command, enabling command injection.
violations.recommendation: Avoid interpolating untrusted GitHub context directly into run scripts. If the title is needed, pass it as an environment variable: env: PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} and then use $PR_TITLE in the script.

violations.description: A secret-bearing file (integration.env) containing a GitHub token was committed to git history.
violations.evidence: git history shows integration.env was added in commit 708f6b7 with content API_TOKEN="[REDACTED_GITHUB_TOKEN]" and deleted in commit 8e01f55. The token is redacted in the diff but the pattern confirms a real credential was committed.
violations.recommendation: Rotate the exposed GitHub token immediately. Use git filter-repo or BFG to purge the file from history, then force-push. Add integration.env to .gitignore to prevent re-committing.

violations.description: Machine-specific absolute path (/Users/developer/project/data) used as default in configuration.
violations.evidence: config.py line 4: DATA_DIR = os.getenv("APP_DATA_DIR", "/Users/developer/project/data") - hardcoded macOS user path.
violations.recommendation: Use a relative path or a platform-agnostic default like './data' or os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'data'), and document APP_DATA_DIR as the override.

violations.description: CI workflow triggers only on pushes to 'release' branch, but the default branch is 'main', so CI never runs on normal pushes.
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml line 4: branches: [release]; git_log shows default branch is 'main'. CI will not trigger on pushes to main.
violations.recommendation: Add 'main' to the push branches filter, e.g. branches: [main, release], so CI runs on the default branch.
